component_findings.dependency_metadata: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-external--part-1--zig): Zig shipped a built-in package manager in version 0.11 in August 2023. It uses build.zig.zon files for manifests and fetches dependencies directly from URLs, usually tarballs on GitHub. There's no central registry yet, though the community runs unofficial indexes like zpm and aquila.
component_findings.distribution_artifacts: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-external--part-1--zig): Score reflects a mixed picture: (a) positive signal - flagship libraries (zap, http.zig, pg.zig, libxev) show genuine, recent, ongoing maintenance activity and explicitly track compiler releases; (b) negative signal - the ecosystem lacks the infrastructure maturity (single registry, download/dependency telemetry, yank/deprecation mechanisms, SBOM/tooling parity) found in longer-established ecosystems, multiple historical package managers were abandoned (gyro, effectively zigmod's original momentum), and package discovery is fragmented across several small, unofficial, scraper-based catalogs rather than one authoritative source. component_findings.registry_discovery: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-external--part-1--zig): No central package registry exists; Zig's built-in package manager fetches dependencies directly from URLs (typically GitHub tarballs), verified by content hash, with no official index.
component_findings.security_provenance: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-external--part-1--zig): The Zig Software Foundation explicitly stays out of package hosting/name-authority governance, and there is no dependency-resolution/download-count transparency comparable to mature registries (npm, crates.io, PyPI).

metric.package_ecosystem_activity_mainte.limitations: No canonical, language-neutral 'total active packages' or 'percent of packages updated in last 12 months' statistic exists for Zig because there is no central registry (explicitly confirmed by multiple sources), so this metric relies on qualitative synthesis of multiple corroborating community sources rather than a single quantitative index, applied with the same retrieval depth as used for domain coverage above.
metric.package_ecosystem_activity_mainte.selection_rule: Use the primary package registry/ecosystem for the language when one exists and evaluate current observable maintenance within the fixed activity window; package count alone is never sufficient.

metric.third_party_library_availability_.candidate_universe: top actively-promoted candidate found via Zigistry/GitHub search for the domain; std.http.Client exists but is standard library, not third-party

component_findings.application_testing: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-external--part-1--zig): Project maturity: This project is production-ready and actively maintained. It provides a comprehensive HTTP client and server implementation. Zig's standard library does not provide HTTP/2, HTTP/3, or QUIC support (per httpx.zig README), so third-party libraries fill an acknowledged std-lib gap.

metric.third_party_library_availability_.limitations: GitHub star counts and forum mentions are used only as declared, consistently-collected corroborating signals per domain, not as the sole proxy for the whole metric; no single popularity number was used standalone. Absence of a central Zig package registry (see package_ecosystem_activity_maintenance evidence) means domain coverage was assessed via community-curated lists (awesome-zig, Zigistry) rather than an authoritative catalog, which is a coverage-measurement limitation shared by this whole metric for Zig.
metric.third_party_library_availability_.selection_rule: Inspect the same five fixed domain groups for every language; prefer the official package index or official ecosystem directory, then independent package/project evidence.
